dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the process-owned op-cert key copy is not left on disk after a hard crash (no atexit/tmpfs/os-level reaper for tempfile.mkdtemp copy).
evidence: keyprov.py:67-68 `runtime_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rebar-opcert-")` then `os.chmod(runtime_dir, 0o700)`
keyprov.py:57-59 `def cleanup(self): ... shutil.rmtree(self.runtime_dir, ignore_errors=True)`
app.py:91-94 cleanup runs only in the lifespan `finally` on graceful shutdown: `signer = getattr(app.state, "signer", None); if signer is not None: signer.cleanup()`

Reachability is bounded: the copy is 0600 within a 0700 process-owned dir, so exposure requires same-user or root; the superseded per-job design also materialized to /tmp. Defense-in-depth gap, not a bright-line leak.
dropped.finding: The process-owned private-key copy (0600 file in a `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rebar-opcert-')` 0700 dir) is only removed by `signer.cleanup()` on GRACEFUL lifespan shutdown; on a hard crash / SIGKILL / OOM the Ed25519 private-key copy persists on disk in a predictable-prefix temp directory with no reaper.
scenarios: opcert service is SIGKILLed/OOM-killed or the container is force-terminated, leaving the private-key copy in /tmp/rebar-opcert-*/opcert-key until the next tmp sweep

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/handle the ownership+mode coupling between the bind-mounted opcert key (0600, host-owned) and the strict 0600 permission check in compose_signer, so a future non-root opcert container does not silently fail startup.
evidence: keyprov.py `_read_path_source`: `if st.st_mode & 0o077:` rejects a bind-mounted key with any group/other read bit
docker-compose.yml:290 `- ./opcert-ed25519-key:/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key:ro` (host-owned, mode 0600 from fetch-secrets.sh:132)
Dockerfile.opcert has no `USER` directive (search for `USER` returned no matches) — container runs as root, so a root process can read a 0600 file regardless of owner
docker-compose.yml:130 comment confirms 'The container runs as root (no USER ...)' is the established pattern
dropped.finding: compose_signer enforces the mounted key be mode 0600-or-stricter (keyprov._read_path_source rejects any group/other bits), and the bind-mounted source is host-owned; this only succeeds because the opcert container runs as root (Dockerfile.opcert sets no USER). A future non-root migration of the opcert service would silently break startup — a 0600 host-owned key would be unreadable by a non-root container UID, and the same-owner assumption of the mode check is undocumented.
scenarios: Hardening the opcert container to a non-root USER later
Host file owned by a UID that differs from the container runtime UID

The change's central AC1 security claim is that compose_signer runs in lifespan BEFORE any queue/worker/network creation so an invalid key makes the app never begin serving; but every app-level test monkeypatches compose_signer to a fake no-op signer, so no test asserts the app REFUSES to start (lifespan raises OpcertKeyError / TestClient enter fails) when composition fails.
